## Should the level-2 walker spec adopt the ankle and knee torques re-sized for the 4,590 kg reference layout?

`DQ-024` · reversibility **easy** · gate G2 · asked 2026-11-13

The torques adopted in DQ-012 (ankle 26.5, knee 22.5 kN m) were sized for a 3,000 kg walker. Re-run on the CL-05 mass (DQ-023), **26.5 kN m of ankle leaves cockpit drops and tips at the envelope corner even with load holding working; 30.5 kN m clears it.** The same rule as before gives ankle 40.5 kN m (1.5 m g L_foot) and knee 26.5 kN m (1.5 times the lowest clearing value, 17.5 kN m), drafted into SYS-016 (sim/results/sizing-cf4.md).

| Option | What it does and costs |
|---|---|
| **Adopt ankle 40.5 and knee 26.5 kN m in the spec** (recommended) | The simulations model a walker that meets SYS-016 again and the envelope clears; the trade study's actuator class grows about 50%. |
| Adopt only the lowest clearing values (ankle 30.5 and knee 17.5 kN m) | Smaller actuators, no margin: the next mass or geometry change re-opens it. |
| Keep 26.5 and 22.5 kN m until the actuation trade closes | No change; the results keep showing the envelope-corner failures. |
